commit_reviews.summary: Adds a well-integrated live-reload dev server that reuses buildSite and extends the existing manual arg-parser pattern rather than introducing new CLI machinery.

compounding_issues: The seed codebase (root index.ts, an unrelated 200-line auth API) was never removed and remains dead debris outside the tsconfig include through all 5 sessions.

Session 2 hand-rolled two template engines (a Handlebars subset and an EJS subset relying on `with(context)` + `Function` eval) inside the monolithic index.ts, creating the god-file that session 4 had to pay down via a large refactor; the dual-engine complexity and eval-based ejs renderer persist.

Session 4's dev-server 'pluginization' is cosmetic: DevServerPlugin is an empty stub class and startDevServer still calls buildSite directly instead of registering lifecycle hooks, so the dev server was never genuinely integrated into the plugin pipeline.

Session 5's incremental cache silently disables render caching whenever any user plugin defines an onFile hook (renderCacheEnabled guard), so caching partially degrades under the plugin system it was built on.

No test was ever executed in any session — npm/npx/pytest were unavailable in the environment — so the growing 116-line Jest suite (including the incremental-cache tests) was never actually validated, accumulating unverified correctness risk across sessions.
key_decisions: Session 1 greenfield: replace the seed with a strict-TypeScript static site generator (package.json/tsconfig/jest setup + markdown parsing + buildSite) rather than extending the auth seed.
Session 2: implement a custom dual template engine (handlebars + ejs subsets) with frontmatter-selected templates/layouts/data instead of adopting an existing templating library.
Session 3: add a dev server with chokidar watch and WebSocket live-reload wired into the CLI as `ssg serve`.

Session 4: decompose the monolith into a plugin architecture with a BuildContext and lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd), an ssg.config.ts loader + defineConfig, and backward-compatible re-export shims (src/server.ts and root plugins/*.ts).
Session 5: content-addressable incremental builds via SHA-256 source/template hashing with a .ssg-cache.json manifest, --incremental/--clean flags, build stats, and plugin-safe cache invalidation.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improves across the five sessions in a clear build-up arc: a modest but correct greenfield foundation, a feature session that adds templating capability while concentrating complexity into one file, an integration session that ships a real operational feature (live-reload dev server), a refactor session that consolidates the monolith into a plugin architecture and cuts index.ts by roughly 70% while preserving backward compatibility, and a final cross-cutting session that adds sophisticated content-hashed incremental caching with targeted tests. The arc moves from merely functional to architecturally structured, though two weak seams persist — the eval-based hand-rolled template engine and the stub dev-server plugin — and the entire suite was never executed due to a missing Node toolchain.
story_review.summary: A coherent, well-sequenced incremental build-out of a static site generator whose quality improves from functional greenfield to plugin-architected with incremental caching, held back only by unvalidated tests, leftover seed debris, and a partially-integrated dev-server plugin.
